question: In Engineering Drawing, which of the following is the correct definition of the term 'dimension'.

options.text: The thickness of the line of a letter
A continuous thick or wide line along which the prints are trimmed
A line that is drawn to make a section evident
A numerical value expressed in an appropriate unit of measurement

solution:
__**Explanation:**__

**Dimension in Engineering Drawing**

**Definition:** In the context of engineering drawing, the term "dimension" refers to a numerical value expressed in an appropriate unit of measurement, which defines the size, shape, or position of a feature of an object. Dimensions are essential for communicating the specifics of a design, ensuring that the object can be accurately manufactured or constructed as intended.

**Purpose of Dimensioning:**

 
• To convey the exact measurements of an object, ensuring consistency and accuracy during manufacturing or construction.
 
• To provide precise information about the size, location, and orientation of features in a design.
 
• To ensure that the design meets functional requirements and fits within the constraints of the intended application.

**Types of Dimensions:**

Dimensions in engineering drawings can be broadly categorized into the following types:

 
• **Linear Dimensions:** These define the straight-line measurements between two points, such as length, width, and height.
 
• **Angular Dimensions:** These specify angles between two lines or surfaces.</l
